html:
Barack Obama was the 44th president of the United States, from 2009 to 2017, and the first African American to hold the office.

He was born in Honolulu, Hawaii, to a white American mother and a Kenyan father, and spent some of his childhood in Indonesia. After Columbia and Harvard Law School, where he was the first Black president of the Harvard Law Review, he worked as a community organiser and lawyer in Chicago. He served in the Illinois state senate and then the US Senate.

He won the presidency in 2008 in the middle of the 2008 financial crisis.

  • A large stimulus law and the rescue of the car industry helped the economy recover.
  • The Affordable Care Act of 2010 extended health insurance to about twenty million more Americans.
  • New rules for banks followed in 2010.
  • In 2011 US special forces killed Osama bin Laden in Pakistan.
  • He signed the Paris climate agreement and reopened ties with Cuba.

He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009. His time in office also saw sharp political division, and his vice president Joe Biden later won the presidency in 2020.
